subject: Hosted evaluation — access acceptance criteria & proposed playbook
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy@finlytics.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Live demo — follow-up & hosted evaluation asks

Thanks for the demo this morning — quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get your hosted evaluation started. Appreciate the clear walkthrough.

Key acceptance criteria (what will make this a successful hosted POC for us):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation < 200ms for single-turn prompts (benchmarking simple Q->A flows).
- Throughput: stable 5 qps average per endpoint during day hours, ability to burst to ~50 qps for peak events (Black Friday characteristics).
- Token economics: we'd like a predictable per-token burn in the sandbox so procurement can estimate costs.
- Security/residency: data stays in the US region for sandbox and logs retained 90 days; audit log access for our compliance team.
- Model control: ability to pin model version + rollback to a previous variant during the eval window.

Operational asks to proceed:
1) A proposed mapping of our logical endpoints to Redwood endpoints (short-chat vs long-response).
2) Suggested rate limits/concurrency defaults for the sandbox and recommended burst policy.
3) Evidence: SOC2 type II summary + list of available audit logs (high level is fine).
4) Sandbox credentials (read/write) and an initial token budget to test batching/prefetch behavior.

I've copied James (ops lead) on the thread — we can share engineer contact names once we confirm next steps.

Next steps from FinLytics: schedule a 45-min technical preflight with your SE, confirm sandbox timeline, and kick off procurement.

Thanks,
Lucy
Lucy Chen
Head of ML Product, FinLytics

Attachments referenced: sample_prod_workload.csv (we attached a small sample of traffic shape in the demo).

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>

Lucy — thanks for the clear summary, and great to see alignment on success criteria. Quick responses below and a proposed next actions list.

Short answers:
- We can meet the latency target for the short-turn flows with our hosted runtime (p95 <200ms) for model sizes similar to the demo; we'll include p95 baselines against your sample traffic in the sandbox run.
- Throughput/burst: sandbox defaults are conservative; we'll propose a two-tier plan (baseline and burst) below.
- Security: will share SOC 2 summary and available audit log formats. Data residency: we will provision your sandbox in the US region.

Attachments: I'm sending two files with this email: inference-access-matrix.csv (endpoint mapping template you can fill) and redwood-playbook-v1.pdf (ops playbook with canary and rate-routing examples).

Proposed sandbox defaults (to start, adjustable after preflight):
- Per-endpoint baseline: 300 requests/min (~5 rps sustained)
- Per-endpoint burst ceiling: 3000 requests/min (~50 rps) with token-based throttling gate
- Token budget: initial trial 100k tokens/day (we can increase for evaluation period)
- Concurrency: default 4 concurrent streams per endpoint; longer-running endpoints bumped to 2 streams with higher token windows

Technical preflight: please propose 2 engineer names and 2 slots for a 45-min call. Ben (SE) will run the preflight and map endpoints to our sandbox topology.

Next actions (proposed):
1) Ben and I run technical preflight with your engineers (this week if possible).
2) We provision sandbox (US) and share credentials + initial token key.
3) You run a 48 hour spike test with provided workload; we collect p95/throughput metrics and iterate on rate limits.
4) Joint review and recommendation for production-facing routing (hosted-only or if you need dedicated capacity).

I'll leave the technical details to Ben below — he'll sketch the endpoint split and canary plan.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Live demo — follow-up & hosted evaluation asks

Alex — notes and technical proposal for the preflight / sandbox mapping. Paste below is the short tech plan I will run on the call.

On the call I'll propose this endpoint mapping (practical, minimizes cold-kv overhead):
- /v1/short-chat (single-turn Q&A, avg tokens out < 80): optimized for low latency; set KV cache TTL to 5 mins; batching window 8–12 ms.
- /v1/long-gen (multi-turn or long form, avg tokens out > 80): favor throughput; batching window 30–60 ms; pin a larger kv cache per session.

Rate and concurrency recommendations for sandbox (start here; we can tune after 48h test):
- Short-chat: baseline 5 qps sustained per endpoint, burst to 50 qps with token-based circuit breaker.
- Long-gen: baseline 2 qps sustained, burst to 15 qps.
- Canary policy: route 10% traffic to new model variant for 24 hours, evaluate latency/error delta, then 50% for 6 hours before full rollout.

Operational controls we'll expose in the sandbox:
- Endpoint-level token/burst knobs in the console (you can change baseline and burst ceilings).
- Automatic fallback to a lighter quantized variant if p95 exceeds 350ms for >5 consecutive minutes.

Preflight checklist I will run on call:
- Confirm sample payloads and sequence lengths from FinLytics (Lucy/Jam es).
- Map logical endpoints to physical endpoints and define session cookie TTLs.
- Provision API keys + role-limited user for your compliance team to view audit logs.

I'll prepare a short test script (curl + node example) you can run to simulate steady-state + burst. Happy to walk through on the call.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
